topicName: Gateway API and Advanced Traffic Routing
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Gateway API and Advanced Traffic Routing in Kubernetes"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Kubernetes Gateway API is the modern evolution of Ingress, providing role-oriented, extensible, and portable routing architecture. This tutorial explores advanced traffic routing patterns using Gateway API."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites and Architecture Overview"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before starting, ensure you have a Kubernetes cluster running with a Gateway API controller installed (such as Envoy Gateway, Istio, or Linkerd). The Gateway API separates concerns into three distinct roles:"},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Infrastructure Provider: Manages GatewayClasses and underlying infrastructure."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Cluster Operator: Manages Gateway objects, binding ports and IPs to infrastructure."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Application Developer: Manages HTTPRoute and other routing resources."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Defining a Gateway"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"First, define a Gateway resource that listens for incoming HTTP traffic on port 80. This acts as the entry point for your cluster traffic."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Gateway
metadata:
  name: external-gateway
  namespace: default
spec:
  gatewayClassName: envoy-gateway
  listeners:
  - name: http
    protocol: HTTP
    port: 80
    allowedRoutes:
      namespaces:
        from: All"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Implementing Canary Routing with HTTPRoute"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Advanced traffic management allows splitting traffic between different versions of an application. The following HTTPRoute shifts 90 percent of traffic to the stable service and 10 percent to the canary service."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata:
  name: app-route
  namespace: default
spec:
  parentRefs:
  - name: external-gateway
    namespace: default
  hostnames:
  - "app.example.com"
  rules:
  - backendRefs:
    - name: app-service-stable
      port: 80
      weight: 90
    - name: app-service-canary
      port: 80
      weight: 10"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 3: Header-Based Routing and Request Splitting"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Gateway API natively supports advanced traffic steering based on headers, query parameters, and methods. Below is an example of routing requests containing a specific header value to the canary backend."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata:
  name: header-route
  namespace: default
spec:
  parentRefs:
  - name: external-gateway
  hostnames:
  - "app.example.com"
  rules:
  - matches:
    - headers:
      - name: "X-Route-Tag"
        value: "beta"
    backendRefs:
    - name: app-service-canary
      port: 80
  - backendRefs:
    - name: app-service-stable
      port: 80"},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"You have successfully configured a Kubernetes Gateway and implemented advanced traffic routing patterns such as weighted canary deployments and header-based routing using the Gateway API."}]
